title: Ecology
subtitle: Who lives where, and why
summary: Twenty-nine reindeer were put on St Matthew Island in 1944. By 1963 there were six thousand, and three years later forty-two. Ecology is about numbers like those, and the nineteen trunk lessons work through the classic cases that explain them: hares and lynx, Paine's sea stars, the finches of Daphne Major in a drought, a forest at Hubbard Brook cut down on purpose, and a curtain hung across Lake 226. Six branches go to collapsed cod stocks and DDT, ant colonies, the Salish Sea shore, Mount St Helens after 1980, the dry side of the Cascades, and salmon in the Elwha and Lake Washington.
